newsitem.title: USA: HP cuts Vectra 500 business computer prices.
newsitem.headline: HP cuts Vectra 500 business computer prices.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co said Monday it is cutting prices of its HP Vectra 500 Series personal computers designed for small businesses by up to 14 percent, effective immediately.
The price cuts are expected to bring the street price of the entry-level HP Vectra 520 5/133 down as low as $1,108, in U.S. dollar terms, in the United States and Canada.
The Vectra personal computer line is designed to meet the core productivity, communications and support needs of small businesses who have no technical support staffs.
The HP Vectra 500 Series PC includes Microsoft Corp's Windows 95 system, with enhanced capabilities including the HP welcome center and HP Internet help and support.
HP and Microsoft Small Business Center also market models of the HP Vectra 500 Series PC which are bundled with Microsoft Office Professional, Microsoft Publisher and Microsoft Plus pre-installed.

The HP 520 5/133 desktop personal computer comes equipped with an Intel Corp 133 megahertz (MHz) Pentium processor, 12 megabytes (MB) of random access memory (RAM), a 1.2 gigabyte (GB) hard drive and a 256 kilobyte (KB) cache.

Models range up to the HP Vectra 525 MCx 5/166 minitower, with a 166-MHz Pentium, 16 MB of RAM, 256 KB cache, a 28.8 Kilobit per second fax/data/voice modem a Matrox Millenium graphics card and Microsoft Office Professional for $1,787.

The Small Business Center HP 525 MCx 5/200 SBC model, equipped with a 200 MHz Pentium, 32 MB of RAM, an eight-speed CR-ROM drive, a 256 KB cache and a 28.8 modem will have an estimated street price of $2,576.
